text:
In a big city lived an old professor named Jahongir. He was the most respected teacher among his students, because his lectures taught not only the knowledge in books, but life itself.

One morning, the professor walked into the lecture hall. In his hands was a large glass jar, and on the table lay a sack of items. The students looked at each other in surprise. What would today’s lesson be about?

Without saying a word, the professor took large rocks from the sack and began placing them into the jar one by one. He arranged them carefully until the jar was filled to the brim. Then he looked at the students and asked:

“Do you think the jar is full?”

“Yes, it’s full,” the students answered.

The professor smiled. He took a handful of small pebbles from the sack and poured them into the jar. When he shook it, the pebbles rolled into the gaps between the large rocks.

“And now? Is the jar full?”

The students hesitated. A girl said quietly, “Maybe it’s full now.”

The professor smiled again. He took a handful of fine sand from the sack and sprinkled it into the jar. The sand filled even the tiniest spaces between the pebbles and rocks.

“And now?”

Everyone fell silent. No one dared to answer anymore.

For the last time, the professor took a cup of water from under the table and began pouring it into the jar. The water soaked into the sand and fit inside. Now the jar was truly full.

“What did you learn from this experiment?” asked the professor.

From the back row, a student named Dilshod raised his hand. “Professor, I get it! No matter how busy we are, if we organize things well, we can fit everything in!”

The professor shook his head and laughed softly. “No, my boy. That’s not the right conclusion. The point is something else.”

Then he emptied the jar, poured everything out onto the table, and continued:

“Watch. Now I’ll try it in reverse order. First the water, then the sand, then the pebbles.”

He did so. The jar quickly filled with water, sand, and pebbles. Then the professor tried to put the large rocks in. But they wouldn’t fit. Not a single one went in.

Silence filled the hall.

“Do you understand now?” said the professor. “This jar is your life. The large rocks are the most important things: your family, your health, your loved ones, love for your parents, your dreams, and your honest path. The pebbles are things that matter but aren’t essential: your job, your house, your car. The sand is everyday trivia: your phone, idle chatter, wasted time. And the water is the empty minutes.

If you fill the jar with sand and water first, there will be no room for the large rocks. Your life will fill up with small things, and you will find no time for what matters most.”

The students lowered their heads in thought. Then Dilshod in the back row raised his hand again.

“Professor, but the jar was full of water. Is there still room for something?”

The professor answered with warmth in his eyes: “A good question. No matter how full the jar is, there is always room for a cup of tea with a friend. Because that, too, is one of the large rocks.”

Everyone in the hall smiled. That day, the students went home and for many years never forgot one question: what is going into my jar first today?

Moral: Life is like a jar with limited space. You can’t fit everything into it. Put the most important things in first: family, health, loved ones. There will be room for the small things. Otherwise, your life will fill up with trivia, and there will be no room left for what is most precious.

tr.title: Banka va toshlar
paragraphs: Katta bir shaharda Jahongir ismli keksa professor dars berar ekan. U o’z talabalari orasida eng hurmatli ustoz ekan, chunki uning darslari faqat kitobdagi bilimlarni emas, hayotni ham o’rgatar ekan.
Bir kuni ertalab professor auditoriyaga kirib kelibdi. Qo’lida katta shisha banka, stol ustida esa bir qop narsa bor ekan. Talabalar ajablanib, bir-biriga qarashibdi. Bugun mavzu nima bo’ladi?

Professor hech narsa demasdan, qopdan katta-katta toshlarni olib, birin-ketin bankaga sola boshlabdi. U toshlarni ehtiyotkorlik bilan joylashtirib, banka og’zigacha to’ldiribdi. Keyin talabalarga qarab so’rabdi:
«Sizningcha, banka to’ldimi?»
«Ha, to’ldi», deb javob berishibdi talabalar.
Professor jilmayibdi. Qopdan bir hovuch mayda shag’al toshlarni olib, bankaga sola boshlabdi. Bankani silkitgan edi, shag’allar katta toshlar orasidagi bo’shliqlarga to’kilib ketibdi.
«Endi-chi? Banka to’ldimi?»
Talabalar bir oz ikkilanibdi. Bir qiz sekin debdi: «Ehtimol, endi to’lgandir.»
Professor yana jilmayibdi. Qopdan bir hovuch mayda qum olib, bankaga sepibdi. Qum shag’al va toshlar orasidagi eng kichik bo’shliqlarni ham to’ldirib ketibdi.
«Va endi?»
Hamma jim qolibdi. Endi hech kim javob berishga jur’at etmabdi.
Professor oxirgi marta stol ostidan bir kosa suv olibdi va bankaga quya boshlabdi. Suv ham qum orasiga singib, bankaga sig’ibdi. Endi banka chindan ham to’la ekan.
«Bu tajribadan nima tushundingiz?» deb so’rabdi professor.
Orqa qatordan Dilshod ismli bir talaba qo’lini ko’taribdi. «Ustoz, men tushundim! Biz qanchalik band bo’lmaylik, agar yaxshi tashkil qilsak, hamma narsaga ulgurish mumkin ekan!»
Professor boshini chayqab, ohista kulibdi. «Yo’q, o’g’lim. Bu to’g’ri xulosa emas. Gap boshqa narsada.»
Keyin u bankani bo’shatib, hammasini stol ustiga to’kibdi va davom etibdi:
«Qaranglar, endi hammasini teskari tartibda solib ko’ramiz. Avval suvni, keyin qumni, keyin shag’alni quyaman.»
U shunday qilibdi. Banka tezda suv, qum va shag’aldan to’lib ketibdi. Keyin professor katta toshlarni bankaga solmoqchi bo’libdi. Lekin ular sig’masmish. Birontasi ham kirmabdi.
Auditoriyada jimlik hukm surib turibdi.

«Endi tushundingizmi?» debdi professor. «Bu banka sizning hayotingiz. Katta toshlar hayotdagi eng muhim narsalar: oilangiz, sog’lig’ingiz, yaqinlaringiz, ota-onangizga bo’lgan mehr, orzularingiz va halol yo’lingiz. Shag’al toshlar ishingiz, uyingiz, mashinangiz kabi muhim, lekin zarur bo’lmagan narsalar. Qum esa kundalik mayda tashvishlar: telefon, bekor suhbatlar, behuda vaqt o’tkazish. Suv esa bo’sh-bo’sh o’tadigan daqiqalar.
Agar siz bankaga avval qum bilan suvni to’ldirsangiz, katta toshlarga joy qolmaydi. Hayotingiz mayda ishlar bilan to’lib ketadi, siz esa eng muhim narsalarga vaqt topa olmay qolasiz.»
Talabalar bosh egib o’ylanibdi. Shunda orqa qatordagi Dilshod yana qo’lini ko’taribdi.
«Ustoz, lekin banka suv bilan to’lgan edi. Shunda ham bir narsaga joy bor ekanmi?»
Professor ko’zlarida mehr bilan debdi: «Yaxshi savol. Banka qanchalik to’la bo’lmasin, har doim bir do’st bilan bir piyola choy ichishga joy topiladi. Chunki bu ham katta toshlardan biri.»
Auditoriyadagi hamma jilmayibdi. O’sha kuni talabalar uyiga qaytib borib, ko’p yillar davomida unutmagan bir narsani o’ylashibdi: bugun mening bankamga nima birinchi bo’lib tushyapti?

Qissadan hissa: Hayot cheklangan banka kabi. Unga hamma narsani sig’dirib bo’lmaydi. Avval eng muhim narsalarni, ya’ni oila, sog’liq va yaqinlarni qo’y. Mayda tashvishlarga esa qolgan joy yetadi. Aks holda, hayoting mayda ishlar bilan to’lib, eng qimmatli narsalarga joy qolmaydi.

quiz.q: The professor first filled the jar with large rocks.
Dilshod understood the lesson correctly the first time.
What do the large rocks represent?
o: The most important things, like family and health

quiz.q: What happened when the professor put water and sand in first?
o: The large rocks would not fit
The water spilled on the floor

quiz.q: There is always room for a cup of ___ with a friend.
